subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Spur Gears: Meshing Teeth
description: One-minute skill: Spur Gears: Meshing Teeth.

hook.text: Two toothed wheels interlock. When one turns clockwise, the other turns counterclockwise.

buildup.text: Spur gears have straight teeth parallel to the shaft. They're the simplest and most common gear type.

discovery.text: A small gear driving a large one multiplies torque. A large driving a small one multiplies speed.

twist.text: Spur gears are noisy at high speed. Each tooth strikes the next with a sharp click as they mesh.

climax.text: Clocks, hand drills, and conveyor belts all use spur gears for reliable, predictable motion.

punchline.text: The simplest gear is still the most used. Teeth never go out of style.

quiz.question: What happens when a small spur gear drives a larger one?
options: Speed increases and torque decreases at the output
Torque increases and speed decreases at the output
Both speed and torque increase at the output
